import re

def parse_line(line):
    # Define the regex pattern for the log line
    pattern = r'(\S+) - - \[(.*?)\] "(GET|POST|PUT|DELETE) (\S+)" (\d+) (\d+|-) (\d+\.\d+)'
    
    # Match the line against the pattern
    match = re.match(pattern, line)
    
    if not match:
        raise ValueError("Line does not match the expected format")
    
    # Extract the fields from the match
    ip = match.group(1)
    time = match.group(2)
    method = match.group(3)
    path = match.group(4)
    status = int(match.group(5))
    bytes = int(match.group(6)) if match.group(6) != '-' else 0
    seconds = float(match.group(7))
    
    # Return the parsed data as a dictionary
    return {
        'ip': ip,
        'time': time,
        'method': method,
        'path': path,
        'status': status,
        'bytes': bytes,
        'seconds': seconds
    }

if __name__ == "__main__":

            'path': '/index.html',
            'status': 200,
            'bytes': 2326,
            'seconds': 0.045
        }
        print("Test passed")
    except AssertionError:
        print("Test failed")
    except ValueError as e:
        print(f"ValueError: {e}")

import re

    # Define the regex pattern for the log line
    pattern = r'(\S+) - - \[(.*?)\] "(GET|POST|PUT|DELETE) (\S+)" (\d+) (\d+|-) (\d+\.\d+)'
    
    # Match the line against the pattern
    match = re.match(pattern, line)
    
    if not match:
        raise ValueError("Line does not match the expected format")
    
    # Extract the fields from the match
    ip = match.group(1)
    time = match.group(2)
    method = match.group(3)
    path = match.group(4)
    status = int(match.group(5))
    bytes = int(match.group(6)) if match.group(6) != '-' else 0
    seconds = float(match.group(7))
    
    # Return the parsed data as a dictionary
    return {

        'time': time,

import re

def parse_line(line):
    # Define the regex pattern for the log line
    pattern = r'(\S+) - - \[(.*?)\] "(GET|POST|PUT|DELETE) (\S+)" (\d+) (\d+|-) (\d+\.\d+)'
    
    # Match the line against the pattern
    match = re.match(pattern, line)
    
    if not match:
        raise ValueError("Line does not match the expected format")
    
    # Extract the fields from the match
    ip = match.group(1)
    time = match.group(2)
    method = match.group(3)
    path = match.group(4)
    status = int(match.group(5))
    bytes = int(match.group(6)) if match.group(6) != '-' else 0
    seconds = float(match.group(7))
    
    # Return the parsed data as a dictionary
    return {
        'ip': ip,
        'time': time,
        'method': method,
        'path': path,
        'status': status,
        'bytes': bytes,
        'seconds': seconds
    }

import re

def parse_line(line):
    # Define the regex pattern for the log line
    pattern = r'(\S+) - - \[(.*?)\] "(GET|POST|PUT|DELETE) (\S+)" (\d+) (\d+|-) (\d+\.\d+)'
    
    # Match the line against the pattern
    match = re.match(pattern, line)
    
    if not match:
        raise ValueError("Line does not match the expected format")
    
    # Extract the fields from the match
    ip = match.group(1)
    time = match.group(2)
    method = match.group(3)
    path = match.group(4)
    status = int(match.group(5))
    bytes = int(match.group(6)) if match.group(6) != '-' else 0
    seconds = float(match.group(7))
    
    # Return the parsed data as a dictionary
    return {
        'ip': ip,
        'time': time,
        'method': method,
        'path': path,
        'status': status,
        'bytes': bytes,
        'seconds': seconds
    }

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Test cases

            'bytes': 2326,
            'seconds': 0.045

import re

def parse_line(line):
    # Define the regex pattern for the log line
    pattern = r'(\S+) - - \[(.*?)\] "(GET|POST|PUT|DELETE) (\S+)" (\d+) (\d+|-) (\d+\.\d+)'
    
    # Match the line against the pattern
    match = re.match(pattern, line)
    
    if not match:
        raise ValueError("Line does not match the expected format")
    
    # Extract the fields from the match
    ip = match.group(1)
    time = match.group(2)
    method = match.group(3)
    path = match.group(4)
    status = int(match.group(5))
    bytes = int(match.group(6)) if match.group(6) != '-' else 0
    seconds = float(match.group(7))
    
    # Return the parsed data as a dictionary
    return {
        'ip': ip,
        'time': time,
        'method': method,
        'path': path,
        'status': status,
        'bytes': bytes,
        'seconds': seconds
    }

import re

def parse_line(line):
    # Define the regex pattern for the log line
    pattern = r'(\S+) - - \[(.*?)\] "(GET|POST|PUT|DELETE) (\S+)" (\d+) (\d+|-) (\d+\.\d+)'
    
    # Match the line against the pattern
    match = re.match(pattern, line)
    
    if not match:
        raise ValueError("Line does not match the expected format")
    
    # Extract the fields from the match
    ip = match.group(1)
    time = match.group(2)
    method = match.group(3)
    path = match.group(4)
    status = int(match.group(5))
    bytes = int(match.group(6)) if match.group(6) != '-' else 0
    seconds = float(match.group(7))
    
    # Return the parsed data as a dictionary
    return {
        'ip': ip,
        'time': time,
        'method': method,
        'path': path,
        'status': status,
        'bytes': bytes,
        'seconds': seconds
    }

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Test cases
    test_line = '127.0.0.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2326 0.045'
    try:
        parsed = parse_line(test_line)
        assert parsed == {
            'ip': '127.0.0.1',
            'time': '10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000',
            'method': 'GET',
            'path': '/index.html',
            'status': 200,
            'bytes': 2326,
            'seconds': 0.045
        }
        print("Test passed")
    except AssertionError:
        print("Test failed")
    except ValueError as e:
        print(f"ValueError: {e}")
def parse_log(text):
    lines = text.splitlines()
    parsed_logs = []
    malformed_lines = []

    for i, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        try:
            parsed_logs.append(parse_line(line))
        except ValueError:
            malformed_lines.append(i)

    return parsed_logs, malformed_lines
def bad_lines(text):
    lines = text.splitlines()
    malformed_lines = []

    for i, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):

            continue

import re

def parse_line(line):
    # Define the regex pattern for the log line
    pattern = r'(\S+) - - \[(.*?)\] "(GET|POST|PUT|DELETE) (\S+)" (\d+) (\d+|-) (\d+\.\d+)'
    
    # Match the line against the pattern
    match = re.match(pattern, line)
    
    if not match:
        raise ValueError("Line does not match the expected format")
    
    # Extract the fields from the match
    ip = match.group(1)
    time = match.group(2)
    method = match.group(3)
    path = match.group(4)
    status = int(match.group(5))
    bytes = int(match.group(6)) if match.group(6) != '-' else 0
    seconds = float(match.group(7))
    
    # Return the parsed data as a dictionary
    return {
        'ip': ip,
        'time': time,
        'method': method,
        'path': path,
        'status': status,
        'bytes': bytes,
        'seconds': seconds
    }

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Test cases
    test_line = '127.0.0.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2326 0.045'
    try:
        parsed = parse_line(test_line)
        assert parsed == {
            'ip': '127.0.0.1',
            'time': '10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000',
            'method': 'GET',
            'path': '/index.html',
            'status': 200,
            'bytes': 2326,
            'seconds': 0.045
        }
        print("Test passed")
    except AssertionError:
        print("Test failed")
    except ValueError as e:
        print(f"ValueError: {e}")
def parse_log(text):
    lines = text.splitlines()
    parsed_logs = []
    malformed_lines = []

    for i, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        try:
            parsed_logs.append(parse_line(line))
        except ValueError:
            malformed_lines.append(i)

    return parsed_logs, malformed_lines
def bad_lines(text):
    lines = text.splitlines()
    malformed_lines = []

    for i, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        try:
            parse_line(line)
        except ValueError:
            malformed_lines.append(i)

    return malformed_lines

import re

def parse_line(line):
    # Define the regex pattern for the log line
    pattern = r'(\S+) - - \[(.*?)\] "(GET|POST|PUT|DELETE) (\S+)" (\d+) (\d+|-) (\d+\.\d+)'
    
    # Match the line against the pattern
    match = re.match(pattern, line)
    
    if not match:
        raise ValueError("Line does not match the expected format")
    
    # Extract the fields from the match
    ip = match.group(1)
    time = match.group(2)
    method = match.group(3)
    path = match.group(4)
    status = int(match.group(5))
    bytes = int(match.group(6)) if match.group(6) != '-' else 0
    seconds = float(match.group(7))
    
    # Return the parsed data as a dictionary
    return {
        'ip': ip,
        'time': time,
        'method': method,
        'path': path,
        'status': status,
        'bytes': bytes,
        'seconds': seconds
    }

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Test cases
    test_line = '127.0.0.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2326 0.045'
    try:
        parsed = parse_line(test_line)
        assert parsed == {
            'ip': '127.0.0.1',
            'time': '10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000',
            'method': 'GET',
            'path': '/index.html',
            'status': 200,
            'bytes': 2326,
            'seconds': 0.045
        }
        print("Test passed")
    except AssertionError:
        print("Test failed")
    except ValueError as e:
        print(f"ValueError: {e}")
def parse_log(text):
    lines = text.splitlines()
    parsed_logs = []
    malformed_lines = []

    for i, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        try:
            parsed_logs.append(parse_line(line))
        except ValueError:
            malformed_lines.append(i)

    return parsed_logs, malformed_lines
def bad_lines(text):
    lines = text.splitlines()
    malformed_lines = []

    for i, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        try:
            parse_line(line)
        except ValueError:
            malformed_lines.append(i)

    return malformed_lines

import re

def parse_line(line):
    # Define the regex pattern for the log line
    pattern = r'(\S+) - - \[(.*?)\] "(GET|POST|PUT|DELETE) (\S+)" (\d+) (\d+|-) (\d+\.\d+)'
    
    # Match the line against the pattern
    match = re.match(pattern, line)
    
    if not match:
        raise ValueError("Line does not match the expected format")
    
    # Extract the fields from the match
    ip = match.group(1)
    time = match.group(2)
    method = match.group(3)
    path = match.group(4)
    status = int(match.group(5))
    bytes = int(match.group(6)) if match.group(6) != '-' else 0
    seconds = float(match.group(7))
    
    # Return the parsed data as a dictionary
    return {
        'ip': ip,
        'time': time,
        'method': method,
        'path': path,
        'status': status,
        'bytes': bytes,
        'seconds': seconds
    }

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Test cases
    test_line = '127.0.0.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2326 0.045'
    try:
        parsed = parse_line(test_line)
        assert parsed == {
            'ip': '127.0.0.1',
            'time': '10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000',
            'method': 'GET',
            'path': '/index.html',
            'status': 200,
            'bytes': 2326,
            'seconds': 0.045
        }
        print("Test passed")
    except AssertionError:
        print("Test failed")
    except ValueError as e:
        print(f"ValueError: {e}")
def parse_log(text):
    lines = text.splitlines()
    parsed_logs = []
    malformed_lines = []

    for i, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        try:
            parsed_logs.append(parse_line(line))
        except ValueError:
            malformed_lines.append(i)

    return parsed_logs, malformed_lines
def bad_lines(text):
    lines = text.splitlines()
    malformed_lines = []

    for i, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        try:
            parse_line(line)
        except ValueError:
            malformed_lines.append(i)

import re

def parse_line(line):
    # Define the regex pattern for the log line
    pattern = r'(\S+) - - \[(.*?)\] "(GET|POST|PUT|DELETE) (\S+)" (\d+) (\d+|-) (\d+\.\d+)'
    
    # Match the line against the pattern
    match = re.match(pattern, line)
    
    if not match:
        raise ValueError("Line does not match the expected format")
    
    # Extract the fields from the match
    ip = match.group(1)
    time = match.group(2)
    method = match.group(3)
    path = match.group(4)
    status = int(match.group(5))
    bytes = int(match.group(6)) if match.group(6) != '-' else 0
    seconds = float(match.group(7))
    
    # Return the parsed data as a dictionary
    return {
        'ip': ip,
        'time': time,
        'method': method,
        'path': path,
        'status': status,
        'bytes': bytes,
        'seconds': seconds
    }

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Test cases
    test_line = '127.0.0.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2326 0.045'
    try:
        parsed = parse_line(test_line)
        assert parsed == {
            'ip': '127.0.0.1',
            'time': '10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000',
            'method': 'GET',
            'path': '/index.html',
            'status': 200,
            'bytes': 2326,
            'seconds': 0.045
        }
        print("Test passed")
    except AssertionError:
        print("Test failed")
    except ValueError as e:
        print(f"ValueError: {e}")
def parse_log(text):
    lines = text.splitlines()
    parsed_logs = []
    malformed_lines = []

    for i, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        try:
            parsed_logs.append(parse_line(line))
        except ValueError:
            malformed_lines.append(i)

    return parsed_logs, malformed_lines
def bad_lines(text):
    lines = text.splitlines()
    malformed_lines = []

    for i, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        try:
            parse_line(line)
        except ValueError:
            malformed_lines.append(i)

    return malformed_lines

def top_paths(entries, n=3):
    from urllib.parse import urlparse
    from collections import Counter

    path_counts = Counter()

    def drop_lowest(self, category, n):
        # Get all scores in the specified category
        scores = []
        for student in self.students:
            for assignment in self.assignments:
                if assignment.category == category:
                    score = self.score(student, assignment)
                    max_points = assignment.max_points
                    scores.append((score, max_points))
        
        # Sort scores by percentage of max_points
        scores.sort(key=lambda x: x[0] / x[1])
        
        # Drop the n lowest scores
        scores = scores[n:]
        
        # Calculate the total score and max points
        total_score = sum(score for score, max_points in scores)
        total_max_points = sum(max_points for score, max_points in scores)
        
        # Return the percentage
        return (total_score / total_max_points) * 100 if total_max_points > 0 else 0

def by_hour(entries):
    from collections import defaultdict
    from datetime import datetime

    hourly_totals = defaultdict(int)

    def to_csv(self):
        # Generate CSV header
        header = "student," + ",".join(self.assignments) + ",percent,letter\n"
        
        # Generate CSV data for each student
        csv_data = []
        for student in sorted(self.students):

            for assignment in self.assignments:

            percent = self.percent(student)
            letter = self.letter_grade(percent)
            student_data.extend([f"{percent:.2f}" if percent is not None else "", letter])

        # Join all lines with newline

import re

def toc(text):
    headings = []
    slug_map = {}
    
    # Regular expression to match markdown headings
    heading_pattern = re.compile(r'^(#{1,6})\s+(.*)$')
    
    for line in text.splitlines():
        match = heading_pattern.match(line)
        if match:
            level = len(match.group(1))
            title = match.group(2)
            slug = generate_slug(title, slug_map)
            headings.append((level, title, slug))
    
    return headings

def generate_slug(title, slug_map):
    base_slug = re.sub(r'[^a-zA-Z0-9]+', '-', title.lower()).strip('-')
    if base_slug not in slug_map:
        slug_map[base_slug] = base_slug
    else:
        count = 2
        while f"{base_slug}-{count}" in slug_map:
            count += 1
        slug_map[base_slug] = f"{base_slug}-{count}"
    
    return slug_map[base_slug]

def to_html(text): import re # Regular expression to find markdown links markdown_link_pattern = r'\[(.*?)\]\((.*?)\)' # Function to replace markdown link with HTML link def replace_link(match): text = match.group(1) url = match.group(2) # Replace double quotes in the URL with " url = url.replace('"', '"') return f'{text}' # Replace all markdown links in the text html_text = re.sub(markdown_link_pattern, replace_link, text) return html_text blocks = text.split('\n\n') # Process each block processed_blocks = [] for block in blocks: # Replace & with &, < with <, and > with > escaped_block = block.replace('&', '&').replace('<', '<').replace('>', '>') # Join lines in the block with one space processed_block = ' '.join(escaped_block.splitlines()) processed_blocks.append(processed_block) # Join blocks with '\n' html = '\n'.join(f'

{block}

' for block in processed_blocks) return html if __name__ == "__main__": # Test cases test_text = "This is a test.\n\nThis is another block.\nIt has multiple lines." expected_html = "

This is a test.

\n

This is another block. It has multiple lines.

" assert to_html(test_text) == expected_html, "Test case failed" print("All tests passed!") def to_html(text): import re # Regular expression to find markdown links markdown_link_pattern = r'\[(.*?)\]\((.*?)\)' # Function to replace markdown link with HTML link def replace_link(match): text = match.group(1) url = match.group(2) # Replace double quotes in the URL with " url = url.replace('"', '"') return f'{text}' # Replace all markdown links in the text html_text = re.sub(markdown_link_pattern, replace_link, text) return html_text import re def toc(text): headings = [] slug_map = {} # Regular expression to match markdown headings heading_pattern = re.compile(r'^(#{1,6})\s+(.*)$') for line in text.splitlines(): match = heading_pattern.match(line) if match: level = len(match.group(1)) title = match.group(2) slug = generate_slug(title, slug_map) headings.append((level, title, slug)) return headings def generate_slug(title, slug_map): base_slug = re.sub(r'[^a-zA-Z0-9]+', '-', title.lower()).strip('-') if base_slug not in slug_map: slug_map[base_slug] = base_slug else: count = 2 while f"{base_slug}-{count}" in slug_map: count += 1 slug_map[base_slug] = f"{base_slug}-{count}" return slug_map[base_slug]

# Library Class Methods

## addBook(isbn, title, copies = 1)
- **Arguments**: 
  - `isbn`: The ISBN of the book.
  - `title`: The title of the book.
  - `copies`: The number of copies to add (default is 1).
- **Throws**: 
  - Throws an error if `copies` is not a positive integer.

## copies(isbn)
- **Arguments**: 
  - `isbn`: The ISBN of the book.
- **Returns**: 
  - The number of copies available for the given ISBN.

## titles()
- **Returns**: 
  - An array of all book titles sorted alphabetically.

def to_html(text): import re # Regular expression to find markdown links markdown_link_pattern = r'\[(.*?)\]\((.*?)\)' # Function to replace markdown link with HTML link def replace_link(match): text = match.group(1) url = match.group(2) # Replace double quotes in the URL with " url = url.replace('"', '"') return f'{text}' # Replace all markdown links in the text html_text = re.sub(markdown_link_pattern, replace_link, text) return html_text blocks = text.split('\n\n') # Process each block processed_blocks = [] for block in blocks: # Replace & with &, < with <, and > with > escaped_block = block.replace('&', '&').replace('<', '<').replace('>', '>') # Join lines in the block with one space processed_block = ' '.join(escaped_block.splitlines()) processed_blocks.append(processed_block) # Join blocks with '\n' html = '\n'.join(f'

{block}

' for block in processed_blocks) return html if __name__ == "__main__": # Test cases test_text = "This is a test.\n\nThis is another block.\nIt has multiple lines." expected_html = "

This is a test.

\n

This is another block. It has multiple lines.

" assert to_html(test_text) == expected_html, "Test case failed" print("All tests passed!") def to_html(text): import re # Regular expression to find markdown links markdown_link_pattern = r'\[(.*?)\]\((.*?)\)' # Function to replace markdown link with HTML link def replace_link(match): text = match.group(1) url = match.group(2) # Replace double quotes in the URL with " url = url.replace('"', '"') return f'{text}' # Replace all markdown links in the text html_text = re.sub(markdown_link_pattern, replace_link, text) return html_text import re def toc(text): headings = [] slug_map = {} # Regular expression to match markdown headings heading_pattern = re.compile(r'^(#{1,6})\s+(.*)$') for line in text.splitlines(): match = heading_pattern.match(line) if match: level = len(match.group(1)) title = match.group(2) slug = generate_slug(title, slug_map) headings.append((level, title, slug)) return headings def generate_slug(title, slug_map): base_slug = re.sub(r'[^a-zA-Z0-9]+', '-', title.lower()).strip('-') if base_slug not in slug_map: slug_map[base_slug] = base_slug else: count = 2 while f"{base_slug}-{count}" in slug_map: count += 1 slug_map[base_slug] = f"{base_slug}-{count}" return slug_map[base_slug]

# Library Class Methods

## addBook(isbn, title, copies = 1)
- **Arguments**: 
  - `isbn`: The ISBN of the book.
  - `title`: The title of the book.
  - `copies`: The number of copies to add (default is 1).
- **Throws**: 
  - Throws an error if `copies` is not a positive integer.

## copies(isbn)
- **Arguments**: 
  - `isbn`: The ISBN of the book.
- **Returns**: 
  - The number of copies available for the given ISBN.

## titles()
- **Returns**: 
  - An array of all book titles sorted alphabetically.

def to_html(text): import re # Regular expression to find markdown links markdown_link_pattern = r'\[(.*?)\]\((.*?)\)' # Function to replace markdown link with HTML link def replace_link(match): text = match.group(1) url = match.group(2) # Replace double quotes in the URL with " url = url.replace('"', '"') return f'{text}' # Replace all markdown links in the text html_text = re.sub(markdown_link_pattern, replace_link, text) return html_text blocks = text.split('\n\n') # Process each block processed_blocks = [] for block in blocks: # Replace & with &, < with <, and > with > escaped_block = block.replace('&', '&').replace('<', '<').replace('>', '>') # Join lines in the block with one space processed_block = ' '.join(escaped_block.splitlines()) processed_blocks.append(processed_block) # Join blocks with '\n' html = '\n'.join(f'

{block}

' for block in processed_blocks) return html if __name__ == "__main__": # Test cases test_text = "This is a test.\n\nThis is another block.\nIt has multiple lines." expected_html = "

This is a test.

\n

This is another block. It has multiple lines.

" assert to_html(test_text) == expected_html, "Test case failed" print("All tests passed!") def to_html(text): import re # Regular expression to find markdown links markdown_link_pattern = r'\[(.*?)\]\((.*?)\)' # Function to replace markdown link with HTML link def replace_link(match): text = match.group(1) url = match.group(2) # Replace double quotes in the URL with " url = url.replace('"', '"') return f'{text}' # Replace all markdown links in the text html_text = re.sub(markdown_link_pattern, replace_link, text) return html_text import re def toc(text): headings = [] slug_map = {} # Regular expression to match markdown headings heading_pattern = re.compile(r'^(#{1,6})\s+(.*)$') for line in text.splitlines(): match = heading_pattern.match(line) if match: level = len(match.group(1)) title = match.group(2) slug = generate_slug(title, slug_map) headings.append((level, title, slug)) return headings def generate_slug(title, slug_map): base_slug = re.sub(r'[^a-zA-Z0-9]+', '-', title.lower()).strip('-') if base_slug not in slug_map: slug_map[base_slug] = base_slug else: count = 2 while f"{base_slug}-{count}" in slug_map: count += 1 slug_map[base_slug] = f"{base_slug}-{count}" return slug_map[base_slug]
